sections.h2: Who does what on a Mercer County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices on West Lexington Street in Harrodsburg handle Mercer County tax. The PVA appraises each parcel, the sheriff takes in the payment, and the county clerk files liens and picks up any bill still open once April 15 passes.

By the sheriff's own account the office collects more than $8,000,000 a year, so tax is a big share of its workload. Houses inside Harrodsburg also get a city bill, explained below.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Mercer County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Mercer sits in the Bluegrass of central Kentucky on roughly 249 square miles of land. The county was cut from Lincoln County, Virginia in 1785 and carries the name of General Hugh Mercer. Harrodsburg, the seat, was the first city formally chartered in what was then Kentucky County, according to Wikipedia. Burgin is the second city, and Salvisa is counted as a census designated place.

Visitors come for Old Fort Harrod State Park, the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill with its 30 or more historic buildings, and Herrington Lake. The Louisville Southern Railroad reached Harrodsburg in 1888. Neighbors are Anderson, Woodford, Jessamine, Garrard, Boyle and Washington counties.

The Census Bureau lists 132 building permits for Mercer County in 2025, so some buyers will compare an older house with a new build.

sections.h2: How big is the Mercer County housing market?
sections.html:
The 2020 count came to 22,641 people, up from 21,331 in 2010, and the Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 23,733. Housing units number 10,824.

The 2020 through 2024 survey adds:

  • Owner occupancy is 75.9 percent.
  • Owners paying a mortgage spend a median $1,373 a month on housing, against $497 for owners with none.
  • Broadband reaches 86.8 percent of households.
  • Workers travel 27.2 minutes on average to reach a job.
  • Density is 90.9 people per square mile, well above the 30.0 to 35.5 seen in Menifee and Metcalfe.

sections.h2: Where do you go in Mercer County to pay, appraise or record?
sections.html:
Contact details from the county pages and the PVA site:

  • Sheriff: bills and payments, at 207 W. Lexington St., with a mailing box at P.O. Box 126, Harrodsburg, KY 40330. Phone (859) 734-4221. Doors are open 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, and a box at the entrance accepts payments left after hours.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption forms. Same street address, P.O. Box 244, phone (859) 734-6330, same weekday schedule.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and delinquent bills. Courthouse address, P.O. Box 426, phone (859) 734-6310.

The PVA site has a public property search with limited detail, and a paid subscription opens the full database.

sections.h2: Why do Harrodsburg homeowners get two tax bills?
sections.html:
A house within Harrodsburg pays two governments. The city sends its own bill, and the county sheriff bundles the county, state, library, extension, soil conservation, health and school taxes. City Hall says mailings go out at the end of September.

Harrodsburg publishes its 2025 levies, quoted per $100 of assessed value:

  • City of Harrodsburg: 0.063
  • Kentucky state: 0.106
  • Mercer County: 0.116
  • Library: 0.064
  • Extension office: 0.042
  • Soil conservation: 0.010
  • Health department: 0.050
  • Mercer County schools: 0.705

The city works a sample: a $200,000 assessment produces $126 of city tax. Levies are revisited annually, so rely on the figures printed on your bill.

sections.h2: When must a Mercer County tax bill be paid?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page lays out this calendar for 2026 bills. It mirrors KRS 134.015, with the county's own wording for the later penalty.

  • Oct. 1 to Nov. 1, 2026: 2 percent comes off.
  • Nov. 2 to Dec. 31, 2026: pay what is printed.
  • January 2027: a 5 percent penalty.
  • Later: a 10 percent penalty, with a further 10 percent sheriff fee on payments made between Feb. 1 and April 15.

Whatever is still open moves to the county clerk when business closes on April 15, 2027. The sheriff asks anyone who gets no bill to phone the office. Bills arrive on a white postcard with a yellow strip, which is easy to mistake for junk mail.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Mercer County value?
sections.html:
Ask for a PVA conference during the inspection window, a 13 day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A conference that ends in disagreement leads to a filing at the county clerk's office, where you state your own figure.

A three person board takes up appeals about a month after the window ends and opens by examining recent sales of similar homes. If you hire someone to speak for you, KRS 133.120 limits the choice to lawyers, CPAs, licensed brokers or appraisers and similar professionals, plus your own employees, and that person needs your written authorization.

Mercer County mixes town lots, farms and acreage on one roll, so choose sales of homes like yours. A farm house on acreage and a town lot do not compare well.

sections.h2: Which Mercer County owners qualify for the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Age 65 or older, or a total disability classification, opens the door, and the exemption covers your own residence. The sheriff's page tells them to call the PVA at (859) 734-6330 if they have not signed up.

KRS 132.810 allows one exemption for each residential unit and treats a mobile home as a unit. Your assessment cannot go up because of the value you write on the application. Disabled owners under 65 reapply yearly, except service connected totally disabled veterans and people found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

sections.h2: What happens if Mercer County tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Once April 15 passes, the clerk issues a certificate of delinquency and a lien attaches. Interest builds at 1 percent monthly, and the clerk (10 percent) and county attorney (20 percent) add their fees. The Department of Revenue's sample turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 at transfer and roughly $1,611 after the attorney's first notice.

Outside buyers may purchase certificates beginning in mid-July. After a sale you pay that buyer, and added fees are possible. Before a sale, payment plans run through the county attorney.

sections.h2: How does the January 1 rule affect a Mercer County sale?
sections.html:
January 1 fixes tax ownership. The Mercer County PVA explains that a buyer who closes later in the year still sees the bill issued to the former owner until the next calendar year, though the office tries to send the new owner a copy based on the recorded deed.

That shapes every closing. A buyer without a bill can ask the sheriff for one, and the contract should name who covers the year's tax. For an older bill at the clerk, ask for a payoff figure before picking a closing date.

faqs.q: Where is a Mercer County tax bill paid?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 207 W. Lexington St. in Harrodsburg, or by mail to P.O. Box 126. Payments can also go in the box at the entrance after closing time.

faqs.q: Does the sheriff also collect Harrodsburg city tax?
faqs.a: No. City Hall bills its own levy, and the sheriff's bill covers county, state and school taxes plus the library, extension, soil and health districts.

faqs.q: When does the early payment discount end?
faqs.a: For 2026 bills the 2 percent discount ends November 1, 2026. After that, the printed amount is due through December 31.

faqs.q: Is there a refund if I qualify for the homestead exemption after paying?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 132.810 entitles a person who qualifies after paying to a refund on the exempt portion.

faqs.q: Whose name is on the bill if I closed after January 1?
faqs.a: The prior owner's, until the next calendar year. A new owner can call the sheriff at (859) 734-4221 for a copy.
